children: Laird Superfood's net sales rose 225% year over year, driven primarily by the Navitas and Terrasoul acquisitions, while earnings moved from a loss to income. Acquired brands contributed $13.1M and $18.4M in net sales, respectively; softness in direct-to-consumer sales partly offset the increase.
¹ Reported as “Sales, net”. ² Reported as “Net income (loss) attributable to common stockholders”. ³ Reported as “Diluted”.
: Fell to 29.6% from 36.5%, primarily due to commodity-cost inflation, fuel and freight charges, and Terrasoul's lower-margin business model.
: E-commerce was 54% of sales, up from 47%, mainly reflecting Terrasoul's e-commerce mix.
: Sales and marketing expenses rose 158%, reflecting higher-volume selling costs, increased staffing and greater online and retail marketing.
